attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post. He is not quoting anyone else.

semantics.note: The normalised claim keeps his 'as far as I can tell' hedge and the causal link, that high running costs explain why OpenAI has no profit. Calling it causal is reasonable. The hedge limits the claim to what he could tell, so it is a qualified judgement, not a firm assertion.

contract.note: The contract fairly treats 'as far as I can tell' as an epistemic hedge and assigns no support or contradiction test. A firm financial test would drop his qualification and add accounting criteria he never stated.

reviews.rationale: This is a hedged causal judgement about OpenAI's profitability, qualified by 'as far as I can tell'. Under the policy, hedged or graded-confidence language is not scored. The contract sets no objective test, and the evidence packet is empty. The claim can't be scored, so the outcome is not_adjudicable.
